messages:
tasha: Noticing elevated TLS handshake failures coming from apac-south starting ~03:04 UTC. Keystore exporter reports repeated `evict_cert` events and KMS unwrap denies tied to an IAM condition on the role binding. Anyone made conditional bindings overnight?
sec-bot: Alert: keystore.eviction.rate high on apac-south (5m avg=12) 7:03 UTC7 rule=KS.EvictionRate. Inc created: INC-KESTORE-3210
raja: I pushed RBAC changes to tighten service-account scope; I added an IAM condition to the `keystore-reader@svc-proxy` binding to expire on 2026-04-01. Might be a bad condition expression for apac projects.
oliver: which condition? I saw something like `request.time < timestamp("2026-04-01T00:00:00Z") && resource.name.startsWith("projects/redwood-apac")`. If our location label is `asia-south1` vs `apac-south`, mismatch could cause denies.	
mina: logs from the keystore agent show the mismatch: ```
2026-03-22T03:06:41Z keystore-agent[42]: unwrap error: AccessDeniedException: condition evaluation failed: resource.labels.location=asia-south1, expression expected apac-south
2026-03-22T03:06:41Z keystore-agent[42]: evict_cert alias=projects/redwood/locations/asia-south1/keyRings/proxy/cryptoKeys/proxy-v2
```
raja: Ugh, I used org shorthand in the condition. My bad. Immediate remediation: remove the condition from that binding or add a separate binding targeting `projects/redwood-apac` principals.
tasha: We need a quick patch that avoids cert loss during short RBAC mistakes. Proposed mitigations: 1) keystore-agent keep current cert in memory for a grace window (default 2 minutes) if unwrap fails 2) fall back to local encrypted disk cache unlocked by node KMS identity 3) telemetry rule to block RBAC PRs that alter keystore-role bindings without a simulated unwrap check
infra-oncall: rolling temporary fix: re-added a non-conditional binding for `keystore-reader:svc-proxy` in apac projects (PR infra#3056 revert). Applied in apac; nodes report unwrap success now.
oliver: audit step: query CloudKMS Audit Logs for any Decrypt calls with methodName=Decrypt where principalName != infra-keystore between 03:00-03:10. If none, this was a deny-only outage.
mina: ran audit: no unexpected decrypts. Only denies from `serviceAccount:keystore-reader@svc-proxy` when condition evaluated to false. No compromised keys.
raja: action items: 1) rollback my RBAC condition (done) 2) add unit/integ `keystore-dryrun` CI job that uses service account tokens per-region to call KMS decrypt (dry-run) 3) update keystore-agent to honor a `--grace-unwrap-duration` so TLS continues for short windows
oliver: also add a lint to the RBAC review bot that flags IAM Conditions referencing shorthand org labels; require explicit project/location values when touching keystore roles.
mina: detection tuning: create alert `keystore.evictions > 5 in 2m` and auto-open incident with runbook link: https://incidents.internal/INC-KESTORE-3210/runbook. For severity mapping: if TLS error rate > 0.5% for public endpoints then sev=high.
raja: follow-up security question: could a malformed IAM Condition be exploited? If someone can write an arbitrary condition, yes, but that requires permission to change IAM. Threat model: unauthorized RBAC changes are high risk; ensure PR approval flows + 2FA + restricted maintainer list for iam.* changes.
tasha: I'll draft a short postmortem and retro for next week. Let's also schedule a small spike for keystore-agent resilience (cache + unlock semantics) and instrument a `keystore-sim` job that runs as part of the RBAC PR CI.
sec-bot: Incident INC-KESTORE-3210 created by sec-bot 7:10 UTC7 severity=medium. Links: https://incidents.internal/INC-KESTORE-3210, https://git.internal/infra/PRs/3056
infra-oncall: closing alert; rollback PR merged. Will monitor metrics for 1 hour.
raja: thanks all 64b3fb3fb. I'll follow up with a clean PR for scoped conditions that use `resource.labels.location` mapping table.
mina: adding tickets: INFRA-987 keystore-agent grace-unwrap; SEC-654 RBAC lint rule; QA-42 keystore-dryrun CI.
